;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Near the [[Villa Somalia]] [[presidential palace]] in [[Mogadishu]], five [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] gunmen attack a SYL hotel. The attack and subsequent shootout kills three civilians, two [[Somalia Armed Forces|soldiers]] and all the attackers. [https://www.cbs17.com/news/armed-men-attack-presidential-residence-in-somalias-capital/ (CBS17)]
*[[2019 Jersey City shooting]]
**Heavy gunfire is exchanged between [[New Jersey State Police|police]] and two shooters in [[Jersey City]], [[New Jersey]]. Six people are killed: a police officer, the shooters, and three people inside a [[kashrut|kosher]] [[supermarket]], which the shooters [[barricade]]d themselves in. Police describe the shooting as an "[[ambush]]". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/jersey-city-shooting-today-active-shooter-police-officer-nj-mlk-drive-new-york-a9241241.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/active-shooter-situation-in-jersey-city-sources-say/2238983/ (NBC New York)]
*[[Iranian involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**Satellite images spot a tunnel system being dug at [[Imam Ali military base]] in eastern [[Syria]], which is controlled by the [[Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran|Iranian military]]; Western intelligence believe the tunnels are being constructed to house their missiles. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/iran-underground-tunnel-missile-storage (Fox News)]

;International relations
*[[Myanmar–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] blacklists four top [[Myanmar|Burmese]] [[Tatmadaw|military]] leaders, including [[Commander-in-Chief of Defence Services|Commander-in-Chief]] [[Min Aung Hlaing]], for their role in the [[Persecution of Muslims in Myanmar|persecution of Rohingya Muslims]] and other minorities. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-myanmar-sanctions/u-s-blacklists-head-of-myanmar-military-for-alleged-rights-abuses-against-rohingya-idUSKBN1YE1XU?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Ostrava hospital attack]] 
**In [[Ostrava]], [[Czech Republic]], a man [[mass shooting|opens fire]] in a hospital's waiting room, killing seven people before fleeing, then shooting himself dead. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-czech-shooting/gunman-kills-six-in-czech-hospital-before-shooting-himself-idUSKBN1YE0P4 (Reuters)]
*''[[Rohingya genocide case]]''
**At the [[International Court of Justice]], [[The Gambia]] presents charges against the government of [[Myanmar]] and its leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]], who traveled to appear in the court. According to the prosecution, the Burmese government is responsible for mass rapes, widespread arson and killings of Rohingya children, among other crimes. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-rohingya-world-court/as-suu-kyi-looks-on-gambia-details-mass-rapes-killings-in-myanmar-idUSKBN1YE0HL?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2017 Saint Petersburg Metro bombing]]
**A military court sentences 10 people to jail terms ranging between 19 and 28 years. The person who is said to have trained the [[suicide bomber]] gets prison for life. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-50729108 (BBC News)]
*[[Impeachment inquiry into Donald Trump]]
**[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] in the [[United States House of Representatives]] unveil two [[articles of impeachment]] against [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]: [[abuse of power]] and [[Obstruction of justice|obstruction]] of [[United States Congress|Congress]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/politics/live-news/impeachment-inquiry-12-10-2019/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Alberto Fernández]] takes the oath of office as [[President of Argentina]] while [[Cristina Fernández de Kirchner]] is sworn in as [[Vice President of Argentina|Vice President]]. [https://www.reuters.tv/l/P3X2/2019/12/10/argentina-s-president-elect-alberto-fernandez-is-sworn-in (Reuters)]
